question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 30% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is always considered as the base value of 100%.

To gain a 30% profit, the Selling Price (SP) must be 100% + 30% = 130% of CP.

SP = 130% of 500

SP = (130 ÷ 100) × 500 = 650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the article = ₹500

Desired Profit = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

 
 
 

 
 

 
 CP = ₹500
 100%

 

 
 
 + 30% Profit

 
 SP = ?
 130%

 SP = CP + Profit = 130% of CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 500 × [(100 + 30) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 500 × (130 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 5 × 130

⇒ SP = 650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

A profit is made when the Selling Price is greater than the Cost Price. The basic formula is Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is calculated on the Cost Price as the base. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.
